cues.zh: 感谢Brilliant.org对PBS Digital Studios的支持。
cues.en: Thanks to Brilliant.org for supporting PBS Digital Studios.

cues.zh: 重复《时空》的格言：永远不是外星人……
cues.en: To repeat the Space Time maxim: It's never aliens...

cues.zh: ……直到真的是为止！
cues.en: ... until it is!

cues.zh: 那么，我们来聊聊“奥陌陌”吧。
cues.en: So, let's talk about 'Oumuamua.

cues.zh: 去年，一位访客来到了我们的内太阳系。
cues.en: Last year, a visitor came to our inner Solar System.

cues.zh: 在我们看来，它就像一个微弱的光点，相对于固定恒星快速移动。
cues.en: To us, it looked like a faint spot of light, moving quickly relative to the fixed stars.

cues.zh: 我们以前已经无数次见过类似的东西：
cues.en: We'd seen similar things countless times before:

cues.zh: 孤独的岩石，太阳系形成时的残留物，
cues.en: lonely rocks, remnants of the formation of our Solar System,

cues.zh: 沿着它们围绕太阳的无尽轨道漂移，凭借反射的光微微闪烁。
cues.en: drifting on their endless orbits around the Sun, and faintly glimmering with its reflected light.

cues.zh: 这类小行星和彗星没什么不寻常的，
cues.en: Nothing unusual about such asteroids and comets,

cues.zh: 但这个物体的特别之处在于它的轨迹。
cues.en: but what made this object special was its trajectory.

cues.zh: 它根本不在围绕太阳的轨道上。
cues.en: It was not in orbit around the Sun at all.

cues.zh: 相反，它似乎是从星际空间坠入的，并且正在返回出去的途中。
cues.en: Rather, it appeared to have fallen in from interstellar space, and was on its way back out again.

cues.zh: 这个天体是1I/2017 U1——更广为人知的名字是“奥陌陌”。
cues.en: The object is 1I/2017 U1 -- better known as 'Oumuamua.

cues.zh: 这是我们首次发现的穿越太阳系的星际空间碎片。
cues.en: It's the first chunk of interstellar space debris we've ever spotted passing through our Solar System.

cues.zh: 当时它引起了理所当然的轰动——甚至我们自己也做了一期关于它的节目！
cues.en: It caused a justifiable stir at the time -- hell, even we did an episode on it!

cues.zh: 但奥陌陌最近又登上了新闻。
cues.en: But 'Oumuamua has been making the news again.

cues.zh: 这次是因为Schmuel Bialy和Avi Loeb的一篇新论文，探讨了奥陌陌可能是……
cues.en: This time, it's for a new paper by Schmuel Bialy and Avi Loeb that investigates the possibility that 'Oumuamua is...

cues.zh: ……外星人！
cues.en: ... aliens!

cues.zh: 或者更准确地说，是一面人造光帆，推测是连接在外星探测器上的。
cues.en: Or, more accurately, an artificial light sail, presumably attached to an alien probe.

cues.zh: 今天在Space Time Journal Club，我想做两件事。
cues.en: Today on Space Time Journal Club, I want to do two things.

cues.zh: 第一，评估这个提议的合理性；第二，谈谈围绕它的媒体炒作。
cues.en: First, assess the plausibility of this proposal, and second, talk about the media hype around it.

cues.zh: 首先，以下是我们对奥陌陌的了解：
cues.en: First up, here's what we know about 'Oumuamua:

cues.zh: 它亮度的变化表明它是一个高度拉长的物体，在太空中翻滚。
cues.en: Its changing brightness suggests it's a highly elongated object, tumbling through space.

cues.zh: 它似乎有几百米长，但只有几十米宽。
cues.en: It appears to be a few hundred meters long, but only a few tens of meters across.

cues.zh: 它可能也是扁平的，也可能不是。
cues.en: It may or may not also be flat.

cues.zh: 这是一根太空法棍，也许是经过了太空三明治机压过。
cues.en: It's a space baguette, perhaps after going through a space sandwich press.

cues.zh: 起初，它偏红的颜色看起来像彗星，但后来它并没有产生彗尾，
cues.en: Initially, its reddish color looked comet-like, but then it didn't produce a cometary tail,

cues.zh: 所以人们推测它一定更像岩石或小行星，至少在表面上是这样。
cues.en: so it was assumed it must be more rocky or asteroid-like, at least on the surface.

cues.zh: 这里有几件奇怪的事！
cues.en: A couple of strange things right there!

cues.zh: 对于小行星或彗星来说，这种几何形状非常不寻常。
cues.en: The geometry is very unusual for an asteroid or comet.

cues.zh: 还有一点令人惊讶的是，我们竟然能观测到一个星际天体。
cues.en: It's also a little surprising that we should have seen an interstellar object at all.

cues.zh: 我们当然预计会有许多太空碎片漂浮在恒星之间，
cues.en: We certainly expect there to be a bunch of space junk floating between the stars,

cues.zh: 它们很可能是在行星系统形成的剧烈早期阶段被抛射出来的。
cues.en: probably ejected in the violent early stages of formation of planetary systems.

cues.zh: 但要想我们与“奥陌陌”相遇这件事有较大可能性，这类天体的数量必须非常庞大——
cues.en: But in order for our encounter with 'Oumuamua to have been likely, that population needs to be huge --

cues.zh: 远远多于我们理论模型所预测的星际碎片。
cues.en: much more interstellar debris than our theoretical models predict.

cues.zh: 这些东西是有点怪，但还没怪到让人怀疑是外星人的地步。
cues.en: Those things are odd, but not odd enough to start assuming aliens.

cues.zh: 但现在“奥陌陌”正在飞出太阳系，它做了一件更奇怪的事：
cues.en: But now that 'Oumuamua is on its way out of the solar system, it's doing something even weirder:

cues.zh: 它似乎在加速。
cues.en: It appears to be accelerating.

cues.zh: 或者说，至少它减速的程度没有太阳引力预期造成的那么大。
cues.en: Or, at least it's not slowing down as much as you'd expect due to the Sun's gravitational pull.

cues.zh: 这种非引力加速在六月的一篇《自然》论文中有报道。
cues.en: This non-gravitational acceleration was reported in a nature paper in June.

cues.zh: 额外的加速度很小，但很明显。
cues.en: The extra acceleration is tiny, but it's clear.

cues.zh: 有什么东西在把这个天体往外推。
cues.en: Something is pushing the body outwards.

cues.zh: 单就这一点而言，还不算特别奇怪。
cues.en: By itself, this wouldn't be anything especially weird.

cues.zh: 彗星在飞离太阳时也会表现出类似的加速。
cues.en: Comets show the same sort of acceleration on their way out from the Sun.

cues.zh: 对它们来说，这是气体逸出的结果。
cues.en: In their case, it's a result of outgassing.

cues.zh: 当太阳加热彗星的后表面时，水冰和冻结气体——即所谓的挥发性物质——会蒸发。
cues.en: As the Sun heats the rear surface of the comet, water ice and frozen gases -- so-called volatiles -- evaporate.

cues.zh: 喷出的气体像喷流一样推动彗星前进。
cues.en: The ejected gases act like jets to propel the comet forward.

cues.zh: 在普通彗星上，气体逸出通常可见，因为阳光会反射随喷流带出的尘埃，
cues.en: In regular comets, the outgassing is typically visible as sunlight reflects off dust carried along with the jets,

cues.zh: 我们看到的便是彗星的彗发和彗尾。
cues.en: and we see it as the comet's coma and tail.

cues.zh: 但奥陌陌没有观测到彗发或彗尾。
cues.en: But no coma or tail was observed in 'Oumuamua.

cues.zh: 而且，气体逸出大概会改变物体的翻滚方式，可奥陌陌的翻滚看起来却很稳定。
cues.en: Also, outgassing should probably change the way the object is tumbling, but 'Oumuamua's tumbling appears consistent.

cues.zh: 所以……呃……是外星人，对吧？
cues.en: So... duh... aliens, right?

cues.zh: 哈佛大学的Bialy和Loeb就是这么提出的。
cues.en: So proposed Bialy and Loeb of Harvard University.

cues.zh: 平心而论，论文本身里，这两位作者并没有说它是外星人，甚至没说它可能是外星人。
cues.en: To be fair, in the paper itself, these authors don't say it's aliens, or even that it's probably aliens.

cues.zh: 他们只是做了几项计算，来表明一种特定解释的合理性：
cues.en: They just do a few calculations to show the plausibility of one particular explanation:

cues.zh: 奥陌陌是一面光帆。
cues.en: that 'Oumuamua is a light sail.

cues.zh: 论证是这样的：
cues.en: This is the argument:

cues.zh: 有某种东西在加速这个物体，却没有可见的彗发或彗尾。
cues.en: Something is accelerating this object with no visible coma or tail.

cues.zh: 看起来不像排气，所以也许是辐射压。
cues.en: It doesn't look like outgassing, so maybe it's radiation pressure.

cues.zh: 太阳自身的光可能在推这个物体，使它加速。
cues.en: The Sun's own light could be pushing on the object, speeding it up.

cues.zh: 事实上，观测到的加速度似乎遵循平方反比定律。
cues.en: In fact, the observed acceleration seems to be following an inverse square law.

cues.zh: 加速度随着距太阳距离的平方而减小。
cues.en: The acceleration is decreasing with the square of the distance from the Sun.

cues.zh: 这正是太阳辐射压会产生的效果。
cues.en: Now, that's exactly what you'd expect for solar radiation pressure.

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，这种平方反比加速度也是排气会产生的效果，
cues.en: Incidentally, this inverse square acceleration is also what you'd expect from outgassing,

cues.zh: 因为排气也取决于太阳辐射的强度。
cues.en: because outgassing also depends on the strength of the Sun's radiation.

cues.zh: 但辐射压这套解释只有在“奥陌陌”极其薄且轻的情况下才成立——
cues.en: But the radiation pressure thing would only work if 'Oumuamua is incredibly thin and light --

cues.zh: 比任何可想象的自然太空物体都更薄、更轻。
cues.en: thinner and lighter than any conceivable natural space object.

cues.zh: 所以……是外星人！
cues.en: Ergo... aliens!

cues.zh: Bialy 和 Loeb 计算出，一块宽 50 米、厚度不到一毫米的薄片，
cues.en: Bialy and Loeb calculate that a 50 meter wide sheet less than a millimeter thick

cues.zh: 由高反射材料制成，会产生观测到的亮度和加速度。
cues.en: and made of a highly reflective material would produce the observed brightness and acceleration.

cues.zh: 那听起来像光帆。
cues.en: That sounds like a light sail.

cues.zh: 这项技术我们已经在尝试了。
cues.en: This is technology that we are playing with already.

cues.zh: 日本的IKAROS光帆在2010年飞往金星，
cues.en: The Japanese IKAROS light sail flew to Venus in 2010

cues.zh: 而Breakthrough Starshot计划正打算用光帆作为我们的首个星际探测器。
cues.en: and the Breakthrough Starshot program is planning to use a light sail as our first interstellar probe.

cues.zh: 光帆假说有可能解释这种加速和奇特形状。
cues.en: The light sail hypothesis potentially explains the acceleration and the weird shape.

cues.zh: 它也可能解释我们为什么能看到东西。
cues.en: It may also explain why we saw something at all.

cues.zh: 鉴于像'Oumuamua这样大小的天然太空碎片在星际之间应该罕见得多，
cues.en: Given that natural space debris the size of 'Oumuamua should be much rarer between the stars,

cues.zh: 如果这不是一次偶然相遇呢？
cues.en: what if this wasn't a chance encounter?

cues.zh: 如果外星人故意把这个探测器发送给我们呢？
cues.en: What if aliens sent this probe to us intentionally?

cues.zh: 让我们回顾一下证据。
cues.en: Let's review the evidence.

cues.zh: 'Oumuamua似乎正以完全符合排气的方式加速飞出太阳系，
cues.en: 'Oumuamua appears to be accelerating out of the solar system in a way completely consistent with outgassing,

cues.zh: 只不过没有可见的排气。
cues.en: except there's no visible outgassing.

cues.zh: 'Oumuamua 的形状对天然天体来说很怪异，
cues.en: 'Oumuamua is weirdly shaped for a natural body,

cues.zh: 而且星际空间垃圾不该多到能让 'Oumuamua 这种东西被偶然发现。
cues.en: and there shouldn't be enough interstellar space junk for something like 'Oumuamua to have been spotted by chance.

cues.zh: 关于这些不寻常的特性，合著者 Avi Loeb 喜欢引用夏洛克·福尔摩斯的话：
cues.en: Regarding these unusual qualities, co-author Avi Loeb is fond of quoting Sherlock Holmes:

cues.zh: “当你排除了所有不可能，剩下的，无论多么难以置信，都必定是真相。”
cues.en: "When you have excluded the impossible, whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth."

cues.zh: 这句话的言下之意是，'Oumuamua 怪异之处的所有其他可能解释都已被排除。
cues.en: The implication of that statement is that all other possible explanations for 'Oumuamua's weirdness have been ruled out.

cues.zh: 那么，真的排除了吗？
cues.en: So, have they?

cues.zh: 我们来看看对 'Oumuamua 行为的非外星解释。
cues.en: Let's look at the non-alien explanations of 'Oumuamua's behavior.

cues.zh: 加速是最怪异的地方，我们就从这儿说起。
cues.en: The acceleration is the weirdest thing, so we'll start there.

cues.zh: 排气是显而易见的替代解释，但那样的话，为什么我们看不到？
cues.en: Outgassing is the obvious alternative, but then, why don't we see it?

cues.zh: 嗯，我提到过，普通彗星的彗发和彗尾是通过阳光经尘埃反射而看到的——
cues.en: Well, I mentioned that in regular comets the coma and tail are seen through sunlight reflected off dust --

cues.zh: 那些微小的矿物颗粒随蒸发的水冰一起被带出。
cues.en: tiny mineral grains that are carried out with the vaporizing ice.

cues.zh: 没有反光尘埃，气体逸出对我们的望远镜来说就是不可见的，但仍可能造成观测到的加速。
cues.en: Without reflective dust, outgassing would be invisible to our telescopes, but could still cause the observed acceleration.

cues.zh: 首次报告这一异常加速的论文提出了几种可能的情形。
cues.en: The paper that first reported the unusual acceleration proposes some plausible scenarios.

cues.zh: 也许该天体尘埃含量很低。
cues.en: Perhaps the object has a low abundance of dust.

cues.zh: 或者，也许它拥有异常大的尘埃颗粒，其反射的光比大量较小颗粒更少。
cues.en: Or, perhaps it has unusually large dust grains that'd reflect less light than lots of smaller grains.

cues.zh: 又或者，表面物质在数千年的星际宇宙射线照射下已熔结成硬壳。
cues.en: Or, perhaps the surface material has been fused into a crust by millennia of exposure to interstellar cosmic rays.

cues.zh: 看不到明显的气体逸出很奇怪，但坦白说，也没那么奇怪。
cues.en: The lack of visible outgassing is weird, but frankly, it's not that weird.

cues.zh: 稍微更奇怪的是，翻滚运动似乎不受气体逸出的影响。
cues.en: Slightly weirder is that the tumbling motion doesn't seem affected by outgassing.

cues.zh: 但除非有人做出恰当的计算，证明翻滚运动必然以可观测的方式发生变化，
cues.en: But until someone does a proper calculation to show that tumbling must change in an observable way,

cues.zh: 这就不是一个严肃的论据。
cues.en: this is not a serious argument.

cues.zh: 然后是“奥陌陌”的形状。你怎么会形成一块形状如此怪异的岩石？
cues.en: Then there's 'Oumuamua's shape. How do you get such a weird shaped rock?

cues.zh: 嗯，不同作者提出了不同的设想。
cues.en: Well, different authors have suggested different scenarios.

cues.zh: 也许它曾被潮汐瓦解——被其母恒星或一颗气态巨行星撕扯开来，
cues.en: Perhaps it was tidally disrupted -- pulled apart by the star or a gas giant from its home system,

cues.zh: 很像苏梅克-列维彗星那样。
cues.en: much like the comet Shoemaker-Levy.

cues.zh: 然后，在那漫长的星际旅程中，它可能通过引力重新聚合成了一个奇特的形状。
cues.en: And then, it may have gravitationally reassembled itself into an odd shape on that very long interstellar journey.

cues.zh: 勒布本人早前的一篇论文中也提出了类似的解释，
cues.en: Loeb himself proposes a similar explanation in an earlier paper,

cues.zh: 并补充说，它或许是由于快速自转而解体，随后又重新聚合。
cues.en: adding that perhaps it broke itself apart due to its rapid rotation before reassembling.

cues.zh: 最后，随机遭遇一块星际太空岩石的可能性究竟有多低？
cues.en: And finally, what about the sheer unlikelihood of a random encounter with an interstellar space rock?

cues.zh: 嗯，要想让我们发现“奥陌陌”这件事显得合情合理，
cues.en: Well, in order for our spotting of 'Oumuamua to have been likely,

cues.zh: 星际空间中“奥陌陌”类太空岩石的数量需要达到我们预期的大约10到100倍。
cues.en: interstellar space needs to contain something like 10 to 100 times the number of 'Oumuamua-like space rocks than we expect.

cues.zh: 我的意思是行星形成过程中被抛射出的太空岩石的预期密度。
cues.en: And by that, I mean the expected density of space rocks that are ejected during the planetary formation process.

cues.zh: 有三个反驳论点：
cues.en: There are three counter-arguments:

cues.zh: 第一，太空碎片可能比我们预期的更多。
cues.en: First, there could be more space debris than we expected.

cues.zh: 例如，恒星可能在死亡时释放它们的奥尔特云。
cues.en: For example, it may be that stars release their Oort clouds when they die.

cues.zh: 如果在我们之前经过的每颗恒星都将庞大的彗星云散入银河系，
cues.en: If every star that passed before us shed its vast cloud of comets into the galaxy,

cues.zh: 那就会有足够多的星际垃圾来解释奥陌陌。
cues.en: that would make plenty enough interstellar trash to explain 'Oumuamua.

cues.zh: 第二种解释：
cues.en: Second explanation:

cues.zh: 也许我们只是碰巧遇到了奥陌陌。
cues.en: Maybe we just got lucky with 'Oumuamua.

cues.zh: 也许星际太空垃圾很稀少，但我们恰好撞上了0.1%、1%或10%的概率。
cues.en: Maybe interstellar space junk is rare, but we caught a 0.1 or 1 or 10 percent chance.

cues.zh: 最后，也许奥陌陌根本不是来自太阳系外，而是来自我们自己的奥尔特云，
cues.en: And finally, perhaps 'Oumuamua isn't from outside our solar system at all, but rather comes from our own Oort cloud,

cues.zh: 并被撞击和/或引力相互作用踢出原有轨道，进入了一条飞向群星的轨迹。
cues.en: and was socked from its orbit by impact and/or gravitational interaction into a trajectory that will send it to the stars.

cues.zh: 我们可以有把握地说，对“奥陌陌”的自然解释仍然合理。
cues.en: We can comfortably say that natural explanations for 'Oumuamua are still plausible.

cues.zh: 但对于外星光帆这一非自然解释，我们真的能这么说吗？
cues.en: Can we really say the same about the unnatural explanation of an alien light sail?

cues.zh: 光帆解释不了一件事，那就是翻滚运动。
cues.en: One thing the light sail doesn't explain is the tumbling motion.

cues.zh: 当然，一个正常工作的探测器不该头尾翻转地旋转，所以也许它是个损坏的探测器。
cues.en: Certainly, a working probe shouldn't be spinning end over end, so perhaps it's a broken probe.

cues.zh: 但如果是这样，那我们就会面临与自然星际碎片相同的丰度问题。
cues.en: But if so, then we have the same abundance problem as with natural interstellar debris.

cues.zh: 星际空间需要布满损坏的光帆——大约相当于银河系中每颗恒星有10^15个探测器。
cues.en: Interstellar space would need to be filled with broken light sails -- something like 10^15 probes per star in the Milky Way.

cues.zh: 光帆假说的另一个问题是速度。
cues.en: The other issue with the light sail hypothesis is the speed.

cues.zh: “奥陌陌”在进入太阳系之前以每秒26公里的速度飞行，
cues.en: 'Oumuamua was traveling at 26 kilometers per second before it entered our Solar System,

cues.zh: 而这对于在银河系中随机绕行的物体来说，是相当典型的速度。
cues.en: and that's a pretty typical speed for a random object orbiting in the Milky Way.

cues.zh: 另一方面，突破摄星计划的光帆目标是达到20%光速，
cues.en: On the other hand, the Breakthrough Starshot light sails are aiming at 20% light speed,

cues.zh: 用20年时间抵达半人马座α星系。
cues.en: for a 20 year journey to the Alpha Cent. system.

cues.zh: 奥陌陌上一次造访恒星系，已是百万年前的事了。
cues.en: It's been a million years since 'Oumuamua's last stellar encounter.

cues.zh: 那么，为什么要造一个以如此蜗牛般速度飞行的探测器呢？这肯定超出了任何派遣它的外星人的寿命。
cues.en: So why build a probe that travels at such a snail's pace, surely beyond the lifespan of any aliens who sent it?

cues.zh: 尤其是当把光帆加速到光速的相当一部分的技术
cues.en: Especially when the technology to accelerate a light sail to a good fraction of the speed of light

cues.zh: 连我们这些原始人类都能掌握的时候。
cues.en: is within the grasp of even us primitive humans.

cues.zh: 可以肯定地说，对奥陌陌的任何非自然解释，仍然不如自然解释来得可能，
cues.en: It's pretty safe to say that any unnatural explanation for 'Oumuamua is still less likely than a natural explanation,

cues.zh: 老实说，我怀疑 Bialy 和 Loeb 也知道这一点。
cues.en: and honestly, I suspect that Bialy and Loeb know that.

cues.zh: 在他们的论文中，他们并没有声称外星光帆是最可能的解释——只是说它是一个合理的解释。
cues.en: In their paper, they don't claim that an alien light sail is the most likely explanation -- just that it's a plausible one.

cues.zh: 问题不在于他们做了分析。
cues.en: The issue isn't that they did the analysis.

cues.zh: 科学家应该可以自由探索边缘想法，只要他们是以科学的方式去做。
cues.en: Scientists should be free to pursue fringe ideas, as long as they do it scientifically.

cues.zh: 问题在于这个想法最终是如何传达给公众的。
cues.en: The issue is how this idea ended up being communicated to the public.

cues.zh: 那我们就来聊聊这个。
cues.en: So let's talk about that.

cues.zh: 奥陌陌的光帆假说最早由 Avi Loeb 在九月下旬发表于《科学美国人》的一篇文章中。
cues.en: The light sail hypothesis for 'Oumuamua was first presented by Avi Loeb in late September, in a Scientific American article.

cues.zh: 一个月后，Bialy 和 Loeb 的论文出现在预印本平台 arXiv 上，
cues.en: A month later, the Bialy and Loeb paper appeared on the preprint arXiv,

cues.zh: 几天之后，Centauri Dreams 和 Universe Today 对此进行了报道。
cues.en: and a few days after that, Centauri Dreams and Universe Today wrote about it.

cues.zh: 在接下来的几周里，许多媒体都跟进报道了这个故事。
cues.en: Over the next couple of weeks, many media outlets picked up the story.

cues.zh: 其中一些文章措辞谨慎，有些甚至带有批评，
cues.en: Some of those articles were measured, and some were even critical,

cues.zh: 但大多数都对我们可能发现了一艘外星飞船这件事兴奋不已。
cues.en: but most were giddy at the possibility that we'd discovered an alien craft.

cues.zh: 作者们的资历被醒目地写进了新闻标题：
cues.en: The credentials of the authors were blared in the headlines:

cues.zh: “哈佛天体物理学家……巴拉巴拉巴拉……外星探测器。”
cues.en: "Harvard astrophysicists... blah blah blah... alien probe."

cues.zh: 虽然这些文章里没有不实之处，但可以说其中存在某种不诚实。
cues.en: While nothing in these articles was untrue, it's arguable that there's some dishonesty here.

cues.zh: 诉诸作者权威似乎是有意挑起这样的反应：
cues.en: The appeal to the authority of the authors seems designed to provoke the reaction,

cues.zh: “既然哈佛科学家都这么说了，那肯定是真的。”
cues.en: "Well, if Harvard scientists say so, then it must be true."

cues.zh: 作者在媒体采访中的回应并没有淡化外星人的可能性。
cues.en: The author responses in media interviews do not downplay the likelihood of aliens.

cues.zh: 比如，那句福尔摩斯的名言。
cues.en: For example, that Sherlock Holmes quote.

cues.zh: 所以，我想问你们：
cues.en: So, my question to you:

cues.zh: 把一种不太可能的科学解读强调到超出其可信程度，这是有害的吗，
cues.en: Is it harmful to emphasize an unlikely scientific interpretation beyond its probable veracity,

cues.zh: 仅仅为了点击量和关注度，
cues.en: just for the sake of clicks and attention,

cues.zh: 还是说，只要没有明显危害，任何让公众接触科学的做法最终都是好事？
cues.en: or is any engagement of the public with science ultimately a good thing, as long as there's no clear harm?

cues.zh: 说实话，我也不知道答案，
cues.en: Honestly, I don't know the answer,

cues.zh: 但我确实知道，奥陌陌是近年来天文学中最引人入胜的发现之一。
cues.en: but I do know that 'Oumuamua is one of the most fascinating discoveries in astronomy in recent times.

cues.zh: 不管它是不是外星人，这很可能是我们首次接触到来自星际时空的自然或非自然居民。
cues.en: Whether or not it's aliens, it's likely our first encounter with the natural or unnatural denizens from interstellar space time.

cues.zh: 你有兴趣了解更多天文学知识吗？
cues.en: Are you interested in learning more about astronomy?

cues.zh: Brilliant 是一个解决问题的网站，教你像科学家一样思考。
cues.en: Brilliant is a problem-solving website that teaches you to think like a scientist.

cues.zh: 你不用被动听讲座，而是通过解决有趣又有挑战性的问题来掌握概念。
cues.en: Instead of passively listening to lectures, you get to master concepts by solving fun and challenging problems.

cues.zh: Brilliant 提供了解决这些问题所需的工具和框架。
cues.en: Brilliant provides the tools and framework you need to tackle these problems.

cues.zh: Brilliant 发人深省的内容，基于将复杂问题拆解成易于理解的小块
cues.en: Brilliant's thought-provoking content, based around breaking up complexities into bite-sized understandable chunks

cues.zh: 将引领你从好奇走向精通。
cues.en: will lead you from curiosity to mastery.

cues.zh: 无论你想了解天文学、量子物理，还是人工神经网络，
cues.en: Whether you want to learn about astronomy, quantum physics, or even artificial neural networks,

cues.zh: 都可以在 brilliant.org/spacetime 学到更多。
cues.en: you can learn more at brilliant.org/spacetime.

cues.zh: 上周我们聊到，可能探测到了首个超对称粒子。
cues.en: Last week, we talked about the possible detection of what may be the first supersymmetric particle.

cues.zh: 在进入评论环节之前，我需要做一个重要更正。
cues.en: Now, before I get to comments, I need to make one big correction.

cues.zh: 感谢 Gustavo Valdiviesso 指出这一点。
cues.en: Thanks to Gustavo Valdiviesso for pointing this out.

cues.zh: 我说过，能量极高的中微子预计无法一路穿过地球。
cues.en: I said that extremely high energy neutrinos aren't expected to make it all the way through the planet.

cues.zh: 所以看到高能陶中微子的衰变产物才会感到意外，
cues.en: Hence the surprise at seeing the decay products of a high-energy tau neutrino

cues.zh: 它看起来径直穿过了地球中心。
cues.en: that had appeared to pass right through the center of the Earth.

cues.zh: 这不对！
cues.en: This ain't right!

cues.zh: 中微子无论能量多高，穿过地球都毫无问题。
cues.en: Neutrinos have no trouble passing through the planet, whatever their energy.

cues.zh: 变化的是中微子振荡。
cues.en: What changes is neutrino oscillations.

cues.zh: 当中微子在太空中穿行时，它会在三种类型之间振荡：
cues.en: As a neutrino travels through empty space, they [sic] oscillate between the three types:

cues.zh: 电子中微子、μ子中微子和τ中微子。
cues.en: electron neutrino, muon neutrino, and tau neutrino.

cues.zh: 振荡的频率取决于中微子微小的质量。
cues.en: The rate of oscillation depends on the tiny mass of the neutrino.

cues.zh: 当穿过物质时，与电磁场的相互作用会改变中微子的有效质量，
cues.en: When passing through matter, interactions with the electromagnetic field change the effective mass of the neutrino

cues.zh: 其过程类似于折射率——折射率会改变光在物质中的速度。
cues.en: by a process analogous to the refractive index, which changes the speed of light in matter.

cues.zh: 这反过来又改变了振荡的概率，并抑制了向τ中微子的振荡。
cues.en: This, in turn, changes the probabilities of oscillation, and suppresses oscillations to tau neutrinos.

cues.zh: 这就是Mikheyev-Smirnov-Wolfenstein（即MSW）效应。
cues.en: This is the Mikheyev-Smirnov-Wolfenstein (or MSW) effect.

cues.zh: 所以，并不是中微子无法穿过这颗行星，
cues.en: So, it's not that neutrinos don't make it through the planet,

cues.zh: 而是它们不会振荡成τ中微子，也不会保持为τ中微子。
cues.en: it's just that they don't oscillate into tau neutrinos or stay as tau neutrinos.

cues.zh: 所以，直接来自正下方的 τ 中微子是极其不可能的。
cues.en: So seeing a tau neutrino coming from directly below is incredibly unlikely.

cues.zh: 因此，有人假设是一个电子中微子或 μ 中微子发生相互作用，产生了超对称的 stau 粒子。
cues.en: Hence, the hypothesis that it was an electron or muon neutrino that interacted to produce a supersymmetric stau particle.

cues.zh: tu-nonna-emiliana 问：如果 SUSY 很简单（只要在开头加个 S），那 Sstring 怎么样？
cues.en: tu-nonna-emiliana asks: if SUSY is easy (just add an S to the start), then how about Sstring?

cues.zh: 嗯，其实现代弦理论依赖于超对称，所以它已经包含了。
cues.en: Well, actually modern string theory relies on supersymmetry, so it's already included.

cues.zh: 在那之前它叫“ting 理论”吗？
cues.en: Was it called "ting theory" before that?

cues.zh: 实际上，弦理论这个名字最初适用于我们所说的玻色弦理论。
cues.en: Actually, the name string theory originally applied to what we call bosonic string theory.

cues.zh: 它只解释了传递力的玻色子，比如引力子和光子。
cues.en: It just explained the force carrying bosons like the graviton and the photon.

cues.zh: 要涵盖费米子，就需要超对称。结果就是超弦理论，
cues.en: To encompass fermions, supersymmetry is needed. The result is superstring theory,

cues.zh: 而如今人们谈论弦理论时，隐含的就是某种形式的超弦理论。
cues.en: and these days some form of superstring theory is implied when people talk about string theory.

cues.zh: 你们很多人注意到，我们为层级问题放在屏幕上的维基百科文本片段里有个笔误。
cues.en: Many of you noticed a typo in the segment of the Wikipedia text that we put on screen for the hierarchy problem.

cues.zh: 上面似乎写着弱力比引力强 1,024 倍。
cues.en: It appeared to say that the weak force is 1,024 times stronger than gravity.

cues.zh: 有些人把这当成了模拟假说的证据。
cues.en: Some of you took that to be evidence for the simulation hypothesis.

cues.zh: 但实际上，只是指数在剪切粘贴时丢了。
cues.en: But actually, it's just that the exponent got lost in the cut and paste.

cues.zh: 应该是强 10 的 24 次方倍。
cues.en: It should have been 10 to the power of 24 times stronger.

cues.zh: Hiccup Haddock 问：
cues.en: Hiccup Haddock asks:

cues.zh: 为什么用冰？
cues.en: Why ice?

cues.zh: 意思是：为什么 IceCube 用冰中的光子探测器，而不是其他材料？
cues.en: As in: Why does IceCube use photon detectors in ice instead of any other material?

cues.zh: 答案很简单：冰是（大致）透明的。
cues.en: Well, the answer's simple enough: Ice is transparent(ish).

cues.zh: 中微子是通过中微子碰撞产生的粒子所发出的切伦科夫辐射来探测的。
cues.en: Neutrinos are detected by the Cherenkov radiation produced by particles produced in neutrino collisions.

cues.zh: 那种辐射在冰中传播一小段距离，到达最近的光子探测器。
cues.en: That radiation travels a short distance through ice to the nearest photon detector.

cues.zh: 同样的相互作用也发生在岩石中，但切伦科夫辐射传不了太远。
cues.en: The same interactions happen in rock, but the Cherenkov radiation doesn't get very far.

cues.zh: 你可以用冰以外的透明材料。
cues.en: You could use transparent materials other than ice.

cues.zh: 比如液态水就很常见，日本的超级神冈中微子探测器就用了它。
cues.en: Liquid water is common, for example, in the Super-Kamiokande neutrino detector in Japan.

cues.zh: 我猜你也可以用一大块玻璃或类似的东西，但那样听起来很贵。
cues.en: I guess you could use a giant cube of glass or similar, but that sounds expensive.

cues.zh: 很多人对 IceCube 在粒子物理学中了不起的贡献印象深刻，
cues.en: Many of you are impressed by Ice Cube's incredible contributions to particle physics,

cues.zh: 以及这位老兄的职业生涯竟然如此多元。
cues.en: and how the guy has had such a diverse career.

cues.zh: 感谢 infectedstyles 和 David M 提醒我 Ice Cube 的经典之作，
cues.en: Thanks to infectedstyles and David M for reminding me of Ice Cube's classic,

cues.zh: 《Straight Outta Lepton》，出自他的“Neutrinos With Attitude”时期。
cues.en: "Straight Outta Lepton", during his "Neutrinos With Attitude" years.

cues.zh: 还有些人觉得我那句“or is it”很有 Vsauce 的味道。
cues.en: And some of you thought my "or is it" was very Vsauce.
